│                        │       │                   62def2d862726 
│                        │       ├ Title           : apt: apt: Remote code execution via hard link reuse during
│                        │       │                    package download retries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : On Debian, Ubuntu, and derivative Linux distributions, an
│                        │       │                   on-path attacker who can manipulate the HTTP traffic
│                        │       │                   (including a malicious mirror or proxy) between an APT
│                        │       │                   client and an archive server triggered by a package
│                        │       │                   install can trick the client into installing an
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled unverified package and achieve remote
│                        │       │                   code execution with root privileges.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The vulnerability is caused by the reuse of hard links and
│                        │       │                    requires the client to follow redirects and retry the
│                        │       │                   download of package files. It requires the client to have
│                        │       │                   a non-zero Acquire::Retries configuration setting; the
│                        │       │                   value 3 is the default starting with Debian 12 (bookworm)
│                        │       │                   and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish), so older releases
│                        │       │                   are unaffected in a default configuration

│                        │       │                   c51730cbb9fb0 
│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: BIND: Denial of Service via unbounded processing of
│                        │       │                   crafted DNS messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In a BIND resolver, inbound DNS protocol messages with a
│                        │       │                   particular structure will result in additional processing,
│                        │       │                    with no limit imposed by BIND.  A DNS message with a
│                        │       │                   maliciously large number of such structures will cause
│                        │       │                   BIND to consume disproportionate amounts of CPU time and
│                        │       │                   memory during processing.
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Arbitrary code execution via GSS-TSIG UDP
│                        │       │                   message replay 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Replaying GSS-TSIG signed UDP messages can result in
│                        │       │                   memory corruption in "`named`".  An attacker who can
│                        │       │                   capture a previously signed UDP message can replay it
│                        │       │                   while the negotiated TSIG key is still valid. By also
│                        │       │                   sending crafted queries to a zone the attacker controls,
│                        │       │                   the attacker may potentially achieve remote code
│                        │       │                   execution.
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Denial of Service via assertion failure during
│                        │       │                    redirect processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A BIND resolver that is configured with both a "redirect"
│                        │       │                   zone and "qname-minimization strict" may abort with an

│                        │       │                   7bac4cfb412df 
│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Denial of service via assertion failure in RPZ
│                        │       │                    query processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A recursive BIND server that receives a query with
│                        │       │                   recursion desired (RD=1) followed by a non-recursive query
│                        │       │                    (RD=0) may exit with an assertion failure, resulting in a
│                        │       │                    denial of service. To be vulnerable, the BIND server must
│                        │       │                    allow recursive queries and have at least two RPZ zones
│                        │       │                   configured: one with the default setting of
│                        │       │                   "recursive-only yes", and the other with "recursive-only
│                        │       │                   no".
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.16.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: BIND: Denial of Service via unbounded processing of
│                        │       │                   crafted DNS messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In a BIND resolver, inbound DNS protocol messages with a
│                        │       │                   particular structure will result in additional processing,
│                        │       │                    with no limit imposed by BIND.  A DNS message with a
│                        │       │                   maliciously large number of such structures will cause
│                        │       │                   BIND to consume disproportionate amounts of CPU time and
│                        │       │                   memory during processing.
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Arbitrary code execution via GSS-TSIG UDP
│                        │       │                   message replay 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Replaying GSS-TSIG signed UDP messages can result in
│                        │       │                   memory corruption in "`named`".  An attacker who can
│                        │       │                   capture a previously signed UDP message can replay it
│                        │       │                   while the negotiated TSIG key is still valid. By also
│                        │       │                   sending crafted queries to a zone the attacker controls,
│                        │       │                   the attacker may potentially achieve remote code
│                        │       │                   execution.
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Denial of Service via assertion failure during
│                        │       │                    redirect processing

│                        │       │                   assertion failure while processing the redirect.

│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       │                   ec5e27f8994de 
│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Denial of service via assertion failure in RPZ
│                        │       │                    query processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A recursive BIND server that receives a query with
│                        │       │                   recursion desired (RD=1) followed by a non-recursive query
│                        │       │                    (RD=0) may exit with an assertion failure, resulting in a
│                        │       │                    denial of service. To be vulnerable, the BIND server must
│                        │       │                    allow recursive queries and have at least two RPZ zones
│                        │       │                   configured: one with the default setting of
│                        │       │                   "recursive-only yes", and the other with "recursive-only
│                        │       │                   no".
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.16.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: BIND: Denial of Service via unbounded processing of
│                        │       │                   crafted DNS messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In a BIND resolver, inbound DNS protocol messages with a
│                        │       │                   particular structure will result in additional processing,
│                        │       │                    with no limit imposed by BIND.  A DNS message with a
│                        │       │                   maliciously large number of such structures will cause
│                        │       │                   BIND to consume disproportionate amounts of CPU time and
│                        │       │                   memory during processing.
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Arbitrary code execution via GSS-TSIG UDP
│                        │       │                   message replay 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Replaying GSS-TSIG signed UDP messages can result in
│                        │       │                   memory corruption in "`named`".  An attacker who can
│                        │       │                   capture a previously signed UDP message can replay it
│                        │       │                   while the negotiated TSIG key is still valid. By also
│                        │       │                   sending crafted queries to a zone the attacker controls,
│                        │       │                   the attacker may potentially achieve remote code
│                        │       │                   execution.
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       │                    redirect processing

│                        │       │                   zone and "qname-minimization strict" may abort with an

│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.16.8-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : bind: bind: Denial of service via assertion failure in RPZ
│                        │       │                    query processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A recursive BIND server that receives a query with
│                        │       │                   recursion desired (RD=1) followed by a non-recursive query
│                        │       │                    (RD=0) may exit with an assertion failure, resulting in a
│                        │       │                    denial of service. To be vulnerable, the BIND server must
│                        │       │                    allow recursive queries and have at least two RPZ zones
│                        │       │                   configured: one with the default setting of
│                        │       │                   "recursive-only yes", and the other with "recursive-only
│                        │       │                   no".
│                        │       │                   This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.16.0 through 9.18.50,
│                        │       │                    9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1
│                        │       │                    through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   25006dc227a36 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       │                   d6d110bdcf5e1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   bf72120b1f34c 
│                        │       ├ Title           : dash: dash: Super-polynomial backtracking in pmatch when
│                        │       │                   libc fnmatch is disabled 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in dash. When built without libc fnmatch,
│                        │       │                    the internal pmatch() matcher implements * by unbounded
│                        │       │                   recursion over candidate positions. A local user who can
│                        │       │                   plant filenames, or otherwise feed that matcher, can make
│                        │       │                   a short multi-star pattern such as *.*.*.*.*.tar.gz
│                        │       │                   consume excessive CPU.

│                        │       │                   42309979a4a99 
│                        │       ├ Title           : dash: dash: Heap out-of-bounds write in conv_escape via
│                        │       │                   undersized Unicode escape reservation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in dash. The printf builtin reserves four
│                        │       │                    bytes before converting a Unicode \u or \U escape, but
│                        │       │                   the multi-byte token can need five or six bytes. A local
│                        │       │                   user who can supply such an escape to dash printf or echo
│                        │       │                   %b, including through dash -c and a positional argument,
│                        │       │                   can write one or two bytes past that reservation.

│                        │       │                   3ee22901c53cc 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   41b0b9d7254ee 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libdm: lvm2: libdm: Denial of Service via uncontrolled
│                        │       │                   recursion in config parser 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libdm. A local attacker could craft a
│                        │       │                   malicious Logical Volume Manager (LVM) metadata
│                        │       │                   configuration with deeply nested structures. This could
│                        │       │                   lead to uncontrolled recursion in the libdm configuration
│                        │       │                   file parser, exhausting the stack and causing any LVM
│                        │       │                   command reading the metadata to crash. This vulnerability
│                        │       │                   results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for affected
│                        │       │                   systems.

│                        │       │                   297eef918f124 
│                        │       ├ Title           : git: The sideband payload is passed unfiltered to the
│                        │       │                   terminal in git 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git is a source code management tool. When cloning from a
│                        │       │                   server (or fetching, or pushing), informational or error
│                        │       │                   messages are transported from the remote Git process to
│                        │       │                   the client via the so-called "sideband channel". These
│                        │       │                   messages will be prefixed with "remote:" and printed
│                        │       │                   directly to the standard error output. Typically, this
│                        │       │                   standard error output is connected to a terminal that
│                        │       │                   understands ANSI escape sequences, which Git did not
│                        │       │                   protect against. Most modern terminals support control
│                        │       │                   sequences that can be used by a malicious actor to hide
│                        │       │                   and misrepresent information, or to mislead the user into
│                        │       │                   executing untrusted scripts. As requested on the
│                        │       │                   git-security mailing list, the patches are under
│                        │       │                   discussion on the public mailing list. Users are advised
│                        │       │                   to update as soon as possible. Users unable to upgrade
│                        │       │                   should avoid recursive clones unless they are from trusted
│                        │       │                    sources.

│                        │       │                   b1837373fd08d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   819cb808de3fd 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   e57c993aad906 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in
│                        │       │                   S4U2Proxy requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT krb5 through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer
│                        │       │                   dereference vulnerability in the KDC's
│                        │       │                   get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while
│                        │       │                   leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A
│                        │       │                   malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send
│                        │       │                   an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed
│                        │       │                   client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded
│                        │       │                   credentials 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that
│                        │       │                   allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by
│                        │       │                    sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send
│                        │       │                   forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info
│                        │       │                   entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API
│                        │       │                   acceptor services, causing denial of service.

│                        │       │                   a30c1d49f3f6e 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch
│                        │       │                   retries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5
│                        │       │                   (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between
│                        │       │                   retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by
│                        │       │                   injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by
│                        │       │                   triggering authentication retries.

│                        │       │                   ad7f7b3555e01 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in
│                        │       │                   lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4
│                        │       │                   and later do not free partially decoded buffers on
│                        │       │                   failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                   of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS
│                        │       │                    messages.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in
│                        │       │                   xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data
│                        │       │                    on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via
│                        │       │                   crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.

│                        │       │                    5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key
│                        │       │                   material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak
│                        │       │                    in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly
│                        │       │                   trigger key decryption failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting
│                        │       │                   dereference of null policy name pointers 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a
│                        │       │                   NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows
│                        │       │                    remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a
│                        │       │                   policy request with an empty policy name that reaches
│                        │       │                   authorization checks or logging code.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS
│                        │       │                    via unbounded RPC XDR allocation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not
│                        │       │                   enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows
│                        │       │                   remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                   kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded
│                        │       │                   memory allocations during XDR decoding.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    GSS-RPC auth flavor switching 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication
│                        │       │                    context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP
│                        │       │                   connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial
│                        │       │                    of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly
│                        │       │                   establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via
│                        │       │                    AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments
│                        │       │                   on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to
│                        │       │                   cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind)
│                        │       │                   via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger
│                        │       │                   authentication failures.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via
│                        │       │                   AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup 
│                        │       ├ Description     : clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT
│                        │       │                   Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of
│                        │       │                   the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic
│                        │       │                    CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service
│                        │       │                   (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large
│                        │       │                   number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries.

│                        │       │                   afdff858edcb4 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                   in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT
│                        │       │                   requests. Each failed request allocates client state that
│                        │       │                   is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout,
│                        │       │                   allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it
│                        │       │                   is reclaimed. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   return values to be sent in plain text.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic
│                        │       │                   ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in
│                        │       │                   MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded
│                        │       │                    element array one entry at a time, which allows remote
│                        │       │                   attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in
│                        │       │                    the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ
│                        │       │                   with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field
│                        │       │                   over TCP.

│                        │       │                   indicator support was added), an authenticated attacker
│                        │       │                   can bypass authentication indicator requirements using an
│                        │       │                   unkeyed checksum in the CAMMAC authdata container.

│                        │       │                   1020d6c92a4cd 
│                        │       ├ Title           : apt: apt: Remote code execution via hard link reuse during
│                        │       │                    package download retries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : On Debian, Ubuntu, and derivative Linux distributions, an
│                        │       │                   on-path attacker who can manipulate the HTTP traffic
│                        │       │                   (including a malicious mirror or proxy) between an APT
│                        │       │                   client and an archive server triggered by a package
│                        │       │                   install can trick the client into installing an
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled unverified package and achieve remote
│                        │       │                   code execution with root privileges.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The vulnerability is caused by the reuse of hard links and
│                        │       │                    requires the client to follow redirects and retry the
│                        │       │                   download of package files. It requires the client to have
│                        │       │                   a non-zero Acquire::Retries configuration setting; the
│                        │       │                   value 3 is the default starting with Debian 12 (bookworm)
│                        │       │                   and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish), so older releases
│                        │       │                   are unaffected in a default configuration

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   e0aa16f4a4d53 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       │                   6c80e07db80cc 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   1eb78540283e8 
│                        │       ├ Title           : brotli: Out-of-Bounds Write in Google Brotli Decoder 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder
│                        │       │                   (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through
│                        │       │                   1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated
│                        │       │                   attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory,
│                        │       │                   disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of
│                        │       │                   service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a
│                        │       │                   crafted Brotli-compressed stream.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries
│                        │       │                   between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available
│                        │       │                   version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

│                        │       │                   8ffd84f434c80 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Heap buffer overflow via attacker-controlled
│                        │       │                    fopen mode string 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax
│                        │       │                   extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in
│                        │       │                   the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the
│                        │       │                   function is attacker controlled.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common
│                        │       │                   GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process
│                        │       │                   user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them
│                        │       │                   through without validation.

│                        │       │                   12facf0f054e1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory
│                        │       │                   traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable
│                        │       │                    entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..",
│                        │       │                   unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a
│                        │       │                   program that uses gettext can make it load a message
│                        │       │                   catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file
│                        │       │                   system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through
│                        │       │                   out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format
│                        │       │                   directives do not match the arguments passed by the
│                        │       │                   program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf
│                        │       │                   family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution
│                        │       │                    with the privileges of the program.  The safety of
│                        │       │                   message catalogs relies on them being installed in
│                        │       │                   trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal
│                        │       │                   bypasses this.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in
│                        │       │                   locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL,
│                        │       │                    LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry
│                        │       │                   to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not
│                        │       │                   cover LANGUAGE.
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not
│                        │       │                   "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also
│                        │       │                   be able to select another installed locale, for example
│                        │       │                   through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that
│                        │       │                   the attacker can place the crafted file in a location
│                        │       │                   readable by the target program, and that the environment
│                        │       │                   crosses a trust boundary without the program running as
│                        │       │                   AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv
│                        │       │                   directive and restricts an account to a forced command;
│                        │       │                   the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

│                        │       │                   7d4beea061761 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc DNS stub resolver: Denial of Service via long
│                        │       │                    search domain in configuration 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment
│                        │       │                   variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly
│                        │       │                   200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26
│                        │       │                   to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the
│                        │       │                   process.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The resolver truncates the search list when copying it
│                        │       │                   into the fixed-size _res.defdname buffer, then asserts
│                        │       │                   that the copy is consistent with the full configuration. 
│                        │       │                   The consistency check compared against the wrong size and
│                        │       │                   did not handle a first entry that does not fit, so a
│                        │       │                   correctly truncated list failed the assertion.  Any
│                        │       │                   process that resolves names through the library is
│                        │       │                   affected, including long-running processes that reload
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf on the next query after it changes. 
│                        │       │                   Search domains are commonly written to /etc/resolv.conf
│                        │       │                   from data received over DHCP or from a VPN server, so an
│                        │       │                   attacker on the local network may be able to trigger this
│                        │       │                   without privileges on the target system, subject to
│                        │       │                   validation by the network configuration software.

│                        │       │                   d2e00678852b5 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Privilege escalation and arbitrary code
│                        │       │                   execution via TOCTOU race condition in dynamic loader 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in
│                        │       │                   the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc)
│                        │       │                   versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to
│                        │       │                   escalate privileges. When expanding $ORIGIN in DT_RPATH
│                        │       │                   for setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs, glibc validates
│                        │       │                   the lexically normalized search path against the trusted
│                        │       │                   directories but then opens the raw, un-normalized path. On
│                        │       │                    systems where the Linux fs.protected_hardlinks sysctl is
│                        │       │                   disabled, a local attacker who hard-links such a program
│                        │       │                   into an attacker-controlled directory and wins a race to
│                        │       │                   replace an intermediate path component with a symbolic
│                        │       │                   link can direct the loader outside the trusted directory,
│                        │       │                   causing it to load an attacker-controlled shared object
│                        │       │                   and execute arbitrary code with the elevated privileges of
│                        │       │                    the program.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Exploitation requires an installed setuid or setgid binary
│                        │       │                    whose DT_RPATH uses $ORIGIN followed by ".." traversal
│                        │       │                   that normalizes into a trusted directory, and the ability
│                        │       │                   to hard-link that binary and win the race by swapping a
│                        │       │                   path component for a symbolic link. Major Linux-based OS
│                        │       │                   distributions ship with fs.protected_hardlinks enabled by
│                        │       │                   default and mitigate the vulnerability.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Local attacker can cause denial of service
│                        │       │                   and information disclosure via stack-based buffer
│                        │       │                   overflow. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A stack-based buffer overflow in the dynamic loader
│                        │       │                   (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through
│                        │       │                    2.44 allows a local attacker to crash or corrupt the
│                        │       │                   memory of setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When such a program's DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with
│                        │       │                   $ORIGIN and is followed by NUL or '/' the loader both
│                        │       │                   reads past the end of the path buffer and writes past the
│                        │       │                   end of a stack-allocated internal buffer. The corrupted
│                        │       │                   loader stack can lead to a loader crash (denial of
│                        │       │                   service) and limited disclosure of process memory.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in
│                        │       │                   strncasecmp 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The strncasecmp function in the GNU C Library 2.24 and
│                        │       │                   later optimized for the Power8 architecture may read one
│                        │       │                   byte beyond the input size limit, which may crash a
│                        │       │                   program when that byte is not readable.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This condition may happen when the input strings to the
│                        │       │                   strncasecmp function are attacker controlled in an
│                        │       │                   application and they match all the way up to the edge of
│                        │       │                   their page and the neighbouring page is either not mapped
│                        │       │                   or is not readable.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Heap buffer overflow via attacker-controlled
│                        │       │                    fopen mode string 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax
│                        │       │                   extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in
│                        │       │                   the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the
│                        │       │                   function is attacker controlled.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common
│                        │       │                   GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process
│                        │       │                   user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them
│                        │       │                   through without validation.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory
│                        │       │                   traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable
│                        │       │                    entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..",
│                        │       │                   unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a
│                        │       │                   program that uses gettext can make it load a message
│                        │       │                   catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file
│                        │       │                   system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through
│                        │       │                   out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format
│                        │       │                   directives do not match the arguments passed by the
│                        │       │                   program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf
│                        │       │                   family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution
│                        │       │                    with the privileges of the program.  The safety of
│                        │       │                   message catalogs relies on them being installed in
│                        │       │                   trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal
│                        │       │                   bypasses this.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in
│                        │       │                   locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL,
│                        │       │                    LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry
│                        │       │                   to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not
│                        │       │                   cover LANGUAGE.
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not
│                        │       │                   "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also
│                        │       │                   be able to select another installed locale, for example
│                        │       │                   through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that
│                        │       │                   the attacker can place the crafted file in a location
│                        │       │                   readable by the target program, and that the environment
│                        │       │                   crosses a trust boundary without the program running as
│                        │       │                   AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv
│                        │       │                   directive and restricts an account to a forced command;
│                        │       │                   the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc DNS stub resolver: Denial of Service via long
│                        │       │                    search domain in configuration 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment
│                        │       │                   variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly
│                        │       │                   200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26
│                        │       │                   to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the
│                        │       │                   process.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The resolver truncates the search list when copying it
│                        │       │                   into the fixed-size _res.defdname buffer, then asserts
│                        │       │                   that the copy is consistent with the full configuration. 
│                        │       │                   The consistency check compared against the wrong size and
│                        │       │                   did not handle a first entry that does not fit, so a
│                        │       │                   correctly truncated list failed the assertion.  Any
│                        │       │                   process that resolves names through the library is
│                        │       │                   affected, including long-running processes that reload
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf on the next query after it changes. 
│                        │       │                   Search domains are commonly written to /etc/resolv.conf
│                        │       │                   from data received over DHCP or from a VPN server, so an
│                        │       │                   attacker on the local network may be able to trigger this
│                        │       │                   without privileges on the target system, subject to
│                        │       │                   validation by the network configuration software.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Privilege escalation and arbitrary code
│                        │       │                   execution via TOCTOU race condition in dynamic loader 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in
│                        │       │                   the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc)
│                        │       │                   versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to
│                        │       │                   escalate privileges. When expanding $ORIGIN in DT_RPATH
│                        │       │                   for setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs, glibc validates
│                        │       │                   the lexically normalized search path against the trusted
│                        │       │                   directories but then opens the raw, un-normalized path. On
│                        │       │                    systems where the Linux fs.protected_hardlinks sysctl is
│                        │       │                   disabled, a local attacker who hard-links such a program
│                        │       │                   into an attacker-controlled directory and wins a race to
│                        │       │                   replace an intermediate path component with a symbolic
│                        │       │                   link can direct the loader outside the trusted directory,
│                        │       │                   causing it to load an attacker-controlled shared object
│                        │       │                   and execute arbitrary code with the elevated privileges of
│                        │       │                    the program.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Exploitation requires an installed setuid or setgid binary
│                        │       │                    whose DT_RPATH uses $ORIGIN followed by ".." traversal
│                        │       │                   that normalizes into a trusted directory, and the ability
│                        │       │                   to hard-link that binary and win the race by swapping a
│                        │       │                   path component for a symbolic link. Major Linux-based OS
│                        │       │                   distributions ship with fs.protected_hardlinks enabled by
│                        │       │                   default and mitigate the vulnerability.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Local attacker can cause denial of service
│                        │       │                   and information disclosure via stack-based buffer
│                        │       │                   overflow. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A stack-based buffer overflow in the dynamic loader
│                        │       │                   (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through
│                        │       │                    2.44 allows a local attacker to crash or corrupt the
│                        │       │                   memory of setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When such a program's DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with
│                        │       │                   $ORIGIN and is followed by NUL or '/' the loader both
│                        │       │                   reads past the end of the path buffer and writes past the
│                        │       │                   end of a stack-allocated internal buffer. The corrupted
│                        │       │                   loader stack can lead to a loader crash (denial of
│                        │       │                   service) and limited disclosure of process memory.

│                        │       │                   aeae6969beb15 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in
│                        │       │                   strncasecmp 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The strncasecmp function in the GNU C Library 2.24 and
│                        │       │                   later optimized for the Power8 architecture may read one
│                        │       │                   byte beyond the input size limit, which may crash a
│                        │       │                   program when that byte is not readable.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This condition may happen when the input strings to the
│                        │       │                   strncasecmp function are attacker controlled in an
│                        │       │                   application and they match all the way up to the edge of
│                        │       │                   their page and the neighbouring page is either not mapped
│                        │       │                   or is not readable.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Heap buffer overflow via attacker-controlled
│                        │       │                    fopen mode string 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax
│                        │       │                   extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in
│                        │       │                   the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the
│                        │       │                   function is attacker controlled.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common
│                        │       │                   GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process
│                        │       │                   user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them
│                        │       │                   through without validation.

│                        │       │                   6bd5fbb056ad2 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory
│                        │       │                   traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable
│                        │       │                    entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..",
│                        │       │                   unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a
│                        │       │                   program that uses gettext can make it load a message
│                        │       │                   catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file
│                        │       │                   system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through
│                        │       │                   out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format
│                        │       │                   directives do not match the arguments passed by the
│                        │       │                   program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf
│                        │       │                   family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution
│                        │       │                    with the privileges of the program.  The safety of
│                        │       │                   message catalogs relies on them being installed in
│                        │       │                   trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal
│                        │       │                   bypasses this.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in
│                        │       │                   locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL,
│                        │       │                    LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry
│                        │       │                   to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not
│                        │       │                   cover LANGUAGE.
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not
│                        │       │                   "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also
│                        │       │                   be able to select another installed locale, for example
│                        │       │                   through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that
│                        │       │                   the attacker can place the crafted file in a location
│                        │       │                   readable by the target program, and that the environment
│                        │       │                   crosses a trust boundary without the program running as
│                        │       │                   AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv
│                        │       │                   directive and restricts an account to a forced command;
│                        │       │                   the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

│                        │       │                   18c59f1da1bfd 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc DNS stub resolver: Denial of Service via long
│                        │       │                    search domain in configuration 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment
│                        │       │                   variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly
│                        │       │                   200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26
│                        │       │                   to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the
│                        │       │                   process.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The resolver truncates the search list when copying it
│                        │       │                   into the fixed-size _res.defdname buffer, then asserts
│                        │       │                   that the copy is consistent with the full configuration. 
│                        │       │                   The consistency check compared against the wrong size and
│                        │       │                   did not handle a first entry that does not fit, so a
│                        │       │                   correctly truncated list failed the assertion.  Any
│                        │       │                   process that resolves names through the library is
│                        │       │                   affected, including long-running processes that reload
│                        │       │                   /etc/resolv.conf on the next query after it changes. 
│                        │       │                   Search domains are commonly written to /etc/resolv.conf
│                        │       │                   from data received over DHCP or from a VPN server, so an
│                        │       │                   attacker on the local network may be able to trigger this
│                        │       │                   without privileges on the target system, subject to
│                        │       │                   validation by the network configuration software.
